components.name: aesgcm
components.description: AES-128-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D, TLS 1.3's 12-byte nonce and 16-byte tag), sealed and opened in place, on AES and carry-less multiply instructions where the CPU has them and constant-time portable code elsewhere.

components.name: cpu
components.description: What the CPU has of the instructions the components use (AES, carry-less multiply, SHA-256, SHA-512, VAES), asked once for the process.

components.name: dns
components.description: DNS wire format (RFC 1035) for a stub resolver without I/O: A and AAAA queries with EDNS0, replies checked against them with CNAME chains and compression pointers bounded, and TCP's length framing.

components.name: ecdsa
components.description: ECDSA signature verification on P-256 and P-384 (FIPS 186-4, SEC 1): strict DER signatures, uncompressed keys checked on the curve, Montgomery field arithmetic with P-256's special reduction and NAF double-scalar multiplies.

components.name: file
components.description: Files on Linux by the kernel's own calls, for components that read the system's configuration: open a path, read a file whole up to a limit, a descriptor closed on drop. Nothing on macOS and Windows.

components.name: http1
components.description: HTTP/1.1 client side (RFC 9112) without I/O: requests written into a buffer, and an incremental response parser that takes any split of the input and hands body bytes back uncopied, for Content-Length, chunked and close-delimited bodies.

components.name: resolve
components.description: Host lookup that never blocks the caller's loop, one API on Linux, macOS and Windows: start, poll, take the addresses, drop to cancel. Linux runs resolver (Go's own resolver) on raw system calls and hands its sockets and deadline to the caller's poll; macOS runs getaddrinfo on a thread; Windows runs GetAddrInfoW on a thread, as Go does; on both, the thread signals through wait, which the caller's poll takes beside its own descriptors.

components.name: resolver
components.description: A stub resolver that behaves as Go's, without I/O: resolv.conf, /etc/hosts and nsswitch.conf parsed as Go parses them, files and DNS ordered as Go orders them, one name's lookup as a state machine (search list, A and AAAA, servers rotated, UDP then TCP, timeouts and attempts), and RFC 6724 address order.

components.name: roots
components.description: Mozilla's trust anchors for TLS servers from NSS's certdata.txt at a release tag (MPL 2.0), with Mozilla's distrust-after dates, embedded as PEM and loaded into an x509::Store; scripts/roots-gen.py rebuilds the file from a newer tag.

components.name: rsa
components.description: RSA signature verification (RFC 8017): RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 and RSASSA-PSS with MGF1 and a salt of the hash's length, SHA-256 or SHA-384, for moduli of 2048 to 4096 bits and exponents of at most 33 bits.

components.name: sha256
components.description: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4), HMAC-SHA256 (RFC 2104) and HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869), with SHA instructions where the CPU has them.

components.name: sha384
components.description: SHA-384 (FIPS 180-4), HMAC-SHA384 (RFC 2104) and HKDF-SHA384 (RFC 5869), with SHA512 instructions where the CPU has them.

components.name: tls
components.description: A TLS 1.3 client (RFC 8446) without I/O: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 with an X25519 key share, ECDSA and RSA-PSS server signatures, SNI, ALPN, HelloRetryRequest, KeyUpdate and close_notify; bytes in any split, application records opened in place in the receive buffer and sealed in place in the pending one.

components.name: trust
components.description: TLS server authentication by the operating system's trust, as Go's crypto/x509 does it: macOS's SecTrustEvaluateWithError and Windows's CertGetCertificateChain with the SSL policy, on a thread a poll loop waits on, and on Linux x509::verify against the system's anchors (its bundle and certificate directories, or SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR, read on raw system calls). system() also loads the anchors themselves on all three: macOS's trust domains with their SSL trust settings, Windows's ROOT store less what is disabled for server authentication or Disallowed.

components.name: wait
components.description: What a poll loop waits on, one type on every system and for every component that works while the loop runs: descriptors (sockets on Windows) and a timeout; block and ready to wait on it with poll or WSAPoll; and on macOS and Windows a pool of at most 32 threads with a cancellable FIFO line, and the close-on-exec pipe or non-inherited loopback socket pair that says the work is done.

components.name: x25519
components.description: X25519 key agreement (RFC 7748): a constant-time Montgomery ladder over five 51-bit limbs.

components.name: x509
components.description: X.509 (RFC 5280) for TLS server authentication without I/O: a strict DER parser that borrows the certificate, a store of trust anchors from PEM or DER, and chain verification for a host at a given time, with paths built through intermediates in any order, name constraints as Go enforces them, bounded depth and signature checks, and the leaf's key for TLS 1.3's CertificateVerify.
